contents.review_scope: Shared pivot binding, exact keys, retained cells, margins, output, accounting and public evidence

checks.objection: Nested index/domain identity and duplicate-cell equality have different signed-zero and NULL semantics.
checks.resolution: Identity calls the existing exact KeyColumn serializer; first_unique and extrema call the existing recursive comparator. NULL-parent traversal preserves hidden-child exclusion. Frozen literal naming fixtures and dedicated signed-zero/parent-null tests cover these distinctions.

checks.objection: Retained cells could keep whole input child domains, copy unchanged values or release credits before output consumers finish.
checks.resolution: Only newly retained indices/first cells or changed extrema call selected native payload take. Replacements build the new credited value before dropping the old one; margins clone already compact owners. Bounded native output retains array credits. Dedicated tests exercise compactness, unchanged-cell pressure, replacement overlap, session drop, cancellation and publication cleanup.

checks.objection: Empty or unsupported shapes could bypass admission, and compatibility outputs could silently lose nested schema or publish failed output.
checks.resolution: Binding validates recursive DTypes, aggregate/fill/margin policy before source execution. Empty output uses the native schema; current selected-row margin semantics are preserved. Public coverage freezes complete schemas and values before execution, checks every supported writer and conversion, checks native/Arrow IPC schema readback, and asserts no output/artifact/certificate on denials. ORC nested output remains explicit denial.

boundaries: Full public and Full43 release-build acceptance is still running.
No speedup, whole-process RSS bound, new pivot spill path or complete reader/codec accounting is claimed.

contents.supportRow:
Relational and DataFrame operations
Current source builds compose admitted relational and unary stages, including static nested payloads/explode, nested key/retained-state operations, exact decimal reductions and accepted analytic ROWS/GROUPS/RANGE frames. Scalar pivot columns bind during execution, including correlated inner scopes. Source builds after published v0.4.0 admit scalar-value subqueries with local and hosted acceptance. They also admit static List/FixedSizeList/Struct pivot index, domain and selected-value roles with complete local workflow, resource and regression acceptance; hosted integration remains pending.
Operation/type coverage is finite. Named windows, variable frame offsets, dynamic-pivot-dependent scalar schemas, lateral relations, nested SUM/MEAN, non-NULL nested fill, nested-index margins, unsupported nested leaves and pivot-state spill remain outside the admitted contracts; nested MIN/MAX margins require a UTF8 index. Broader adapters and scalar pivot’s 128-field, type and memory boundaries remain.

app.name: Cloudflare Workers and Pages
app.description: The **Cloudflare GitHub App** automatically deploys your code to Cloudflare when you merge a pull request to your GitHub repository. It can also create a new repository on your GitHub account when you get started with a Cloudflare template. This integration also: - Displays the status of your deployments as check runs - Posts links to preview URLs as comments on each pull request (Cloudflare Pages only) For more information, refer to the [Cloudflare Workers docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/) and [Cloudflare Pages docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/git-integration/).
